title: Drop the Budget’s HMRC tax gap package
name: Drop the Budget’s HMRC tax gap package
noun: dropping the HMRC tax gap package
headline: Drop the HMRC package. Costs £2.0bn in 2029-30.
description: The Budget pays for 670 more HMRC compliance officers and £70 million of debt collection, and lets HMRC take small unpaid debts from the bank accounts of people who can pay but will not. The Treasury scores the package at £2.0 billion in 2029-30, rising to £3.2 billion. Switch this on to drop it and give up that yield from April 2027.

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.

Compliance yield arrives late and is hard to audit: HMRC’s own figures for what it collects are estimates of what would otherwise have gone unpaid, and the OBR rates this package’s costing as highly uncertain (October 2026 outlook, Table 3.3).

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
